la-la-land.overview: A jazz pianist and an aspiring actress fall in love while pursuing their dreams in Los Angeles, only to find that success and romance may be incompatible. Chazelle's ravishing musical is a love letter to the city, to old Hollywood, and to the bittersweet cost of ambition.

reviews.quote: A gorgeous, old-fashioned enchantment that scrapes away the lacquer of nostalgia to find something achingly true underneath.
Chazelle has made a series of films about artists who sacrifice everything. This one counts the cost.

goodfellas.overview: The rise and fall of Henry Hill inside the New York mob, told at breakneck speed. Scorsese's kinetic masterpiece redefined the gangster film with its propulsive editing, revolutionary soundtrack curation, and Liotta's magnetic narration. Essential big-screen viewing for the Copacabana tracking shot alone.

reviews.quote: No finer film has ever been made about organized crime — not even The Godfather.
Scorsese's mob epic is so tightly wound, so exhilarating, you almost forget you're watching psychopaths.

pulp-fiction.overview: Interlocking tales of hitmen, a boxer, a gangster's wife, and a pair of diner bandits collide across Los Angeles. Tarantino's Palme d'Or winner rewired American cinema with its non-linear storytelling, crackling dialogue, and deep-cut soundtrack. A film that invented a new vernacular for movies.

reviews.quote: A series of post-modern, overlapping stories that are both exhilarating and appalling, funny and profound.
Tarantino's masterpiece is a series of interlocking tales told with electrifying wit and bottomless movie love.

interstellar.overview: A former NASA pilot traverses a wormhole near Saturn in search of a new home for humanity. Nolan's IMAX-shot space epic is cinema at its most physically overwhelming — the docking sequence, the wave planet, the time dilation heartbreak. See it on the biggest screen possible.

reviews.quote: Nolan's most ambitious film is a humbling, awe-inspiring vision of what cinema can do when it reaches for the infinite.
A movie that wears its heart on its sleeve, often to powerful effect — an intimate epic about love across dimensions.

jurassic-park.overview: A paleontologist, a chaos theorist, and two kids fight for survival when a theme park's cloned dinosaurs break free. Spielberg's landmark blockbuster still holds up as pure cinema — the T. rex attack remains one of the greatest sequences ever staged. The mix of practical effects and early CGI is unmatched.

reviews.quote: Spielberg delivers the ultimate thrill ride — an adventure so primal it taps into childhood wonder and terror in equal measure.
It is a true movie milestone, presenting awe and terror that is completely convincing.

gone-girl.overview: When his wife vanishes on their fifth anniversary, a man becomes the prime suspect in a case that unravels into something far darker. Fincher's ice-cold thriller is a masterclass in misdirection, with Rosamund Pike delivering one of the great screen villains of the 21st century.

reviews.quote: Fincher's razor-sharp adaptation is a toxic love story that doubles as a media satire of lacerating intelligence.
A brilliantly nasty entertainment that takes a wrecking ball to the institution of marriage.

everything-everywhere-all-at-once.overview: A Chinese-American laundromat owner discovers she must connect with parallel universe versions of herself to save the multiverse. The Daniels' genre-smashing Oscar winner is maximalist filmmaking with a beating heart — simultaneously absurdist comedy, martial arts epic, and the most moving mother-daughter story in recent memory.

reviews.quote: A maximalist explosion of creativity that somehow resolves into the most tender film about a mother-daughter relationship in years.
An exuberant swirl of genre anarchy held together by a big, beating heart and Michelle Yeoh's magnificent performance.

tampopo.overview: A truck driver helps a widowed ramen shop owner perfect her noodle recipe, while vignettes celebrate the sensuality of food. Itami's 'ramen western' is a one-of-a-kind cinematic experience — part spaghetti western homage, part food porn, part meditation on how eating connects us to pleasure, death, and love.

reviews.quote: The first Japanese noodle western — an utterly unique comedy that celebrates food as an expression of love, art, and life.

paterson.overview: A bus driver in Paterson, New Jersey writes poetry in a notebook during his lunch breaks. Jarmusch's quietly radical film celebrates the beauty of routine and small creative acts. Adam Driver delivers one of his most subtle performances in a movie that argues the most extraordinary thing is paying attention to ordinary life.

reviews.quote: A film of quietly accumulating enchantment — Jarmusch finds the poetry in the ordinary and makes it extraordinary.
Jarmusch's most gentle and profound film, a hymn to the inner creative life that sustains us all.

the-godfather.overview: The aging patriarch of an organized crime dynasty transfers control to his reluctant youngest son. Coppola's operatic adaptation of Puzo's novel is the defining American epic — Gordon Willis's candlelit cinematography, Nino Rota's haunting score, and Brando's iconic performance create cinema's most complete world.

reviews.quote: The Godfather is told entirely within a closed world, and that's what makes it so chilling — it's a story of American ambition warped by loyalty.
The greatest gangster film ever made, and one of the most influential narrative films of all time.
The rare Apatow-produced comedy where the sentimentality doesn't feel forced — it's genuinely, messily human.

10-things-i-hate-about-you.overview: A new kid at school recruits the only guy tough enough to date the meanest girl on campus so he can date her younger sister. Gil Junger's Shakespeare-via-Seattle teen comedy is a time capsule of late-90s perfection, elevated by Heath Ledger's star-making performance and a killer soundtrack.

reviews.quote: Heath Ledger's incandescent charm powers a teen comedy that's smarter and more literate than it has any right to be.

wicked-for-good.overview: The conclusion of the two-part adaptation of the beloved Broadway musical, following Elphaba and Glinda through the events that transform them into the Wicked Witch and the Good Witch of Oz.

reviews.quote: Jon M. Chu completes his dazzling adaptation with a finale that earns its emotional crescendo through spectacle and sincerity in equal measure.
A rare romantic film that takes Black love seriously and gives it the lush, literary treatment it deserves.

days-and-nights-in-the-forest.overview: Four middle-class men from Calcutta escape to the countryside, where their pretensions slowly unravel in encounters with the locals. Ray's masterful ensemble piece is a quiet demolition of class privilege and male entitlement, shot with his signature humanist precision.

reviews.quote: Ray strips away the veneer of urban sophistication to reveal the petty cruelties and self-deceptions lurking underneath.

queen-kelly.overview: A convent girl is seduced by a prince, only to be exiled to an African brothel in this legendarily troubled silent epic. Gloria Swanson's real-life feud with director von Stroheim over this film became the basis for Sunset Boulevard. A fascinating fragment of Hollywood excess.

reviews.quote: A fascinatingly incomplete relic of silent-era excess, with Swanson giving a remarkable performance under von Stroheim's lavish direction.

baby-face.overview: A young woman from a small town sleeps her way to the top of a New York bank. Stanwyck's pre-Code masterpiece is astonishingly frank about female sexuality and ambition — the camera literally tilts up the floors of the skyscraper as she conquers each level. Essential pre-Code cinema.

reviews.quote: Stanwyck is magnificent, playing a woman who weaponizes her sexuality with a cold, clear-eyed pragmatism that still shocks.
Altman at his most anarchic and inventive — a wild, unclassifiable fable about the dream of flight and American freedom.
A fitfully entertaining but deeply confused finale that mistakes fan service for storytelling.
Brando gives one of the most naked performances in cinema history, but the film's exploitative treatment of Schneider casts a long shadow.
Korine has made a neon-drenched fever dream that is simultaneously a celebration and an indictment of American excess.
Schwarzenegger at his wisecracking best, in a dystopian thriller that now looks eerily prescient about reality television.
An audacious, blackly funny cannibal western with one of the great unsung film scores — Damon Albarn and Michael Nyman's music is genius.
A wartime screwball delight with Jean Arthur at her most effervescent, capped by one of the great seduction scenes in Hollywood history.
Guest's gentle mockumentary about folk music is his warmest film — the satire comes with genuine affection.
Guest's gentle mockumentary about folk music is his warmest film — the satire comes with genuine affection.
Sorvino and Kudrow are a sublime comic duo — their chemistry lifts this cult favorite into the stratosphere.

podcasts.episode: Romy and Michele's High School Reunion

reviews.quote: The critical consensus missed what audiences didn't — a perfectly time-capsuled 90s hangout movie with an irresistible soundtrack.
Wertmuller's savage, grotesque masterwork — Giannini's performance is one of the great feats of physical acting.
Reese Witherspoon tears through this deranged Little Red Riding Hood update with a ferocity that announced a major talent.
Fellini deliberately empties Casanova of all romance, creating a magnificent, grotesque pageant of joyless seduction.
Fellini deliberately empties Casanova of all romance, creating a magnificent, grotesque pageant of joyless seduction.
Kaufman's lush adaptation captures bohemian Paris with a sensuality that earned the first-ever NC-17 rating.
Wesley Snipes gives a galvanizing performance as Nino Brown — a crack-era kingpin drawn with pulp energy and real menace.
Campion renders the Keats-Brawne romance with a luminous, tactile beauty — you can practically feel the fabric of the costumes.
Fosse's directorial debut overflows with kinetic choreography and MacLaine's unstoppable energy, even when the story falters.
Pasolini's ribald, earthy adaptation celebrates the human body and carnal joy with a painter's eye.
A psychedelic masterpiece of Hungarian animation — a swirling cosmos of myth and color unlike anything else in cinema.
George Miller's dark, visionary sequel is that rare children's film willing to confront cruelty and sorrow head-on.
Lupino's taut, ruthless thriller is a landmark — the first American film noir directed by a woman, and one of the leanest ever made.
Wiseman's patient, immersive documentary reveals how a great museum lives and breathes — it's a meditation on art itself.
Lucas's debut is a stark, chilling vision of a dehumanized future — all the more impressive for its micro-budget ingenuity.
Boorman's delirious sci-fi folly is either a misunderstood masterpiece or a magnificent disaster — possibly both at once.
Martel's masterful period film transforms colonial waiting into existential dread — a slow-burn of extraordinary power.
Whatever its narrative shortcomings, Belly is one of the most visually stunning crime films ever shot — every frame is a painting.
Midler and Hershey generate genuine warmth and chemistry, elevating a shameless tearjerker into something truly affecting.
Lyne's adaptation is more faithful to the novel than Kubrick's, trading icy satire for a disturbing, uncomfortably beautiful sensuality.
Russ Meyer's outrageous, fast-paced B-movie is a feminist action film decades ahead of its time — Tura Satana is an icon.
Early Meyer — crude but kinetic, already showing his singular obsession with strong women and desert landscapes.
Franco's dreamlike, jazz-soaked adaptation is one of his most atmospheric and controlled films — genuinely mesmerizing.
Bunuel's masterpiece of bourgeois desire and repression remains genuinely subversive — Deneuve has never been better.
One of the great films about the unknowability of desire — Bunuel leaves you permanently uncertain about what is real and what is fantasy.
Ryan Coogler delivers a Southern Gothic vampire film that doubles as a meditation on the Blues, Black American identity, and the bargains we make with evil.
Bold, genre-bending filmmaking from a director at the peak of his powers.
Hitchcock's most purely terrifying film — the absence of explanation makes the horror existential.
A masterwork of sustained dread that transforms the natural world into a source of incomprehensible menace.
The great British horror film — a folk musical that slowly tightens into a trap of pagan dread.
A unique and disturbing film that works because it takes its paganism completely seriously.
A charming Irish fantasy with groundbreaking special effects — the young Sean Connery is magnetic even in a supporting role.
Phil Lord and Chris Miller deliver a thrilling sci-fi adventure that combines the survival ingenuity of The Martian with a genuinely moving interspecies friendship.
Gordon Parks Jr.'s Harlem drug epic is elevated by Curtis Mayfield's transcendent soundtrack — arguably the greatest in film history.
Neil Jordan's lush, gothic adaptation is a feast for the senses — Cruise and Pitt make for an unexpectedly electric vampire duo.
Whale's expressionist masterpiece still startles — Karloff's Monster remains the most sympathetic creation in horror history.
Stevens' sprawling Texas epic is one of the great American films about wealth, race, and the passage of time — Dean's final performance is extraordinary.
Bunuel's Palme d'Or winner is a savage, blasphemous parable about charity and hypocrisy that was banned by Franco's Spain.
Winterbottom and Coogan create a giddy, unreliable memoir of Manchester's music scene — Joy Division through the Hacienda and beyond.
Weird Al's sole starring vehicle is a gleefully anarchic cult comedy — a lo-fi UHF broadcast of pure absurdist joy.
The most devastating animated film ever made — Takahata's wartime masterpiece is an unflinching portrait of innocence consumed by war.
An animated film of startling emotional power, ranking with the greatest anti-war films ever made.
Busby Berkeley's Technicolor fever dream reaches a hallucinatory peak with the banana number — pure cinema delirium.
Wiseman's observational camera reveals the authoritarian rituals of a Philadelphia high school with devastating clarity.
A gorgeous animated love letter to Cuban jazz and the music that survived exile — the visual style is as seductive as the soundtrack.
Sembene's landmark film — the first feature by a sub-Saharan African director — is a devastating, concise indictment of colonial exploitation.
Varda's playful, profound documentary about gleaning — collecting what others leave behind — is really about art, aging, and the beauty of looking.
Bigger, crazier, and somehow more cinematic than the original — there's a strange purity to Knoxville and crew's commitment to pain.
A rare animated sequel that deepens its characters — the peacock villain is stunning, and Po's backstory is surprisingly emotional.
A time capsule of San Francisco's late-90s rave scene — captures the communal euphoria and idealism of dance culture with genuine affection.
The Muppets' third film has a real New York energy — the wedding finale is one of the great feel-good moments in the franchise.
Nair's debut is a neo-realist portrait of Mumbai street children that never condescends — raw, compassionate, and unforgettable.
Reitman's debut is a razor-sharp satire of spin culture — Aaron Eckhart is brilliantly loathsome as Big Tobacco's smoothest operator.
Fassbinder's tender, devastating Sirkian melodrama about an aging cleaning woman and a Moroccan guest worker is one of the great love stories in cinema.
A film of remarkable emotional precision — Fassbinder strips social prejudice bare with Brechtian clarity and Sirkian warmth.
Cassavetes' penultimate film is his most nakedly autobiographical — a raw, devastating study of love as both salvation and destruction.
Kon's final film is a dazzling, reality-bending animation that directly inspired Inception — but is wilder, funnier, and more inventive.
Haneke's ice-cold provocation forces the audience to confront their own complicity in screen violence — the fourth-wall breaks are devastating.
De Palma's most outrageously Hitchcockian thriller — a lurid, virtuosic exercise in voyeurism that doubles as a love letter to sleazy 80s Hollywood.
Jodorowsky's psychedelic, blasphemous masterpiece is cinema as occult ritual — an assault on every sense that somehow achieves transcendence.
Keene's austere, haunting Icelandic fairy tale gave Bjork her first screen role — a stark, beautiful debut of remarkable visual intelligence.
Blaustein's documentary pulls back the curtain on pro wrestling with empathy and unflinching honesty — the Mick Foley family scenes are heartbreaking.
The ultimate midnight movie — a gloriously trashy rock musical that liberated a generation of misfits and invented audience participation.
Teshigahara's unsettling identity thriller asks what it means to wear a face — Kafkaesque body horror rendered with cool, clinical beauty.
Akerman's glacially beautiful adaptation of Proust is a study in obsessive love — the slowness is the point, and it's hypnotic.
Cocteau's 1946 masterpiece transforms fairy tale into pure cinema — Alekan's cinematography creates a world of genuine enchantment.
Visconti's late masterpiece is a melancholy chamber piece about an aging professor whose isolation is shattered by a chaotic family — Burt Lancaster is magnificent.

the-lord-of-the-rings-the-fellowship-of-.overview: The definitive version of Jackson's epic — a hobbit inherits a ring of immense power and begins a perilous journey across Middle-earth. The extended cut adds 30 minutes of world-building that deepen every character and location. On a big screen, this is one of the most immersive cinematic experiences ever created.

reviews.quote: Jackson's extended edition of Fellowship is the definitive version — the additional footage deepens the world-building and emotional stakes considerably.
One of the great achievements in fantasy filmmaking — a world conjured with such detail and conviction it feels like history, not fiction.

halloween-h20-20-years-later.overview: Twenty years after the events of Halloween night, Laurie Strode is living under an assumed identity when Michael Myers tracks her down. Jamie Lee Curtis's triumphant return transforms a formulaic sequel into something with real emotional stakes.

reviews.quote: Jamie Lee Curtis's return elevates a slick but formulaic slasher sequel — her final-act transformation from victim to warrior is genuinely thrilling.

the-apostle.overview: A Pentecostal preacher on the run from the law reinvents himself in a small Louisiana town. Duvall wrote, directed, financed, and delivered one of cinema's most complex portraits of faith — a man who is simultaneously a genuine holy man and a dangerously flawed human being.

reviews.quote: Duvall wrote, directed, financed, and stars in one of the great American performances — a preacher both charismatic and deeply flawed.

hustlers.overview: Inspired by a viral New York Magazine article, a crew of strippers turns the tables on their Wall Street clients. Lorene Scafaria's electric crime drama features Jennifer Lopez's career-best performance and a killer structure — Goodfellas for the strip club set.

reviews.quote: Lorene Scafaria's electric crime drama is powered by Jennifer Lopez's career-best performance — a Goodfellas for the strip club set.

poetic-justice.overview: A young postal worker and aspiring poet joins a road trip from South Central to Oakland, finding unexpected romance along the way. Singleton's gentler follow-up to Boyz n the Hood pairs Janet Jackson and Tupac Shakur in a tender love story set against everyday Black Los Angeles.

reviews.quote: Singleton's follow-up to Boyz n the Hood is a gentler, more romantic film — Janet Jackson and Tupac have an unlikely, genuine chemistry.

lemony-snicket-s-a-series-of-unfortunate.overview: Three orphans are placed in the care of their distant relative Count Olaf, a theatrical villain determined to steal their fortune. Jim Carrey's unhinged performance and the film's handcrafted, Edward Gorey-inspired production design make it a delightfully dark family film.

reviews.quote: Jim Carrey's unhinged Count Olaf is a marvel, and the film's gloomy, handcrafted production design gives it a dark fairy-tale texture Hollywood rarely attempts.

dreams.overview: Eight vignettes based on Kurosawa's actual dreams, from a child's encounter with a fox wedding to a walk through a Van Gogh painting. The last film of cinema's greatest visual storyteller at his most personal and painterly — every frame is a canvas.

reviews.quote: Kurosawa's late anthology film is pure visual poetry — eight dreams rendered with the painterly grandeur of a master at the end of his career.

race-for-your-life-charlie-brown.overview: Charlie Brown and the Peanuts gang head to summer camp for a whitewater raft race. The third animated Peanuts feature captures the gentle melancholy and dry humor that makes Schulz's world endure.

reviews.quote: The third Peanuts feature is a breezy summer camp adventure — lighter than its predecessors but still carries that gentle Schulzian melancholy.
Isabela Merced is an absolute delight, and the film is far smarter and funnier than it has any right to be — a genuinely enjoyable family adventure.

law-of-desire-on-35mm.overview: Early Almodovar at his most passionate — a gay film director becomes entangled in an obsessive love triangle with a stalker and a transsexual actress. The film that announced Antonio Banderas as a force. On 35mm, the saturated colors glow.

reviews.quote: Early Almodovar at his most passionate and transgressive — Antonio Banderas explodes onto screen in a role of furious, obsessive desire.

peaky-blinders-the-immortal-man.overview: Tommy Shelby's saga reaches the big screen as Cillian Murphy reprises his iconic role in the cinematic conclusion to the Peaky Blinders story. A chance to see the Birmingham gangster epic rendered at full theatrical scale.

reviews.quote: Cillian Murphy brings Tommy Shelby to the big screen with the brooding intensity fans expect — a fitting cinematic send-off for the Peaky Blinders saga.

obsessed.overview: A successful asset manager's life is thrown into turmoil when a temp worker begins to stalk him. A shameless Fatal Attraction update elevated by Beyonce and Ali Larter going full camp in the climactic fight scene.

reviews.quote: A guilty-pleasure thriller elevated entirely by Beyonce's ferocious screen presence — the final fight scene is worth the price of admission.

batch-81.overview: Filipino university students endure an increasingly brutal fraternity initiation process. Mike De Leon's 1982 masterpiece is a thinly-veiled allegory for authoritarianism under Marcos — one of the essential films of Philippine cinema.

reviews.quote: Mike De Leon's harrowing Filipino drama about fraternity hazing is a thinly-veiled allegory for Marcos-era authoritarianism — brutal, essential viewing.

cloak-and-dagger-keeper-of-the-flame.overview: A wartime double feature: Fritz Lang's espionage thriller about nuclear scientists and George Cukor's dark drama about a journalist investigating a national hero's death. Two Hollywood masters grappling with WWII-era paranoia and propaganda.

reviews.quote: A fascinating double bill of wartime thrillers — Lang's spy adventure and Cukor's dark political drama make for a revealing Hollywood WWII pairing.

avalanche.overview: Zeki Demirkubuz's raw, unflinching drama about a man consumed by jealousy after his wife's betrayal. Part of the Turkish New Wave that brought social realism and moral complexity to a national cinema ready for reinvention.

reviews.quote: A bracing early work from Zeki Demirkubuz, part of the Turkish New Wave that reinvigorated national cinema with raw social realism.

gossip-girl-best-of-b-s.overview: The best episodes of the Blair and Serena saga on the big screen. A curated theatrical experience celebrating the Upper East Side friendship that defined a generation of prestige teen television.

reviews.quote: Blair and Serena's dynamic remains the beating heart of Gossip Girl — their friendship is the rare TV relationship that justifies every plot twist.
